Oppelt et al. [@oppelt2018model] also measured the TNFα response under drugs causing liver
injury: diclofenac (DCF) with the imaging and blots of the first chapters, and amiodarone (AMD),
paracetamol (APAP), fialuridine (FIAU) and ximelagatran (XIM) with four blots. Which pathway
processes does each compound change? The publication answered this for DCF alone, with an L1
penalty on the differences of all rate constants between treated and untreated cells, scanned over
the penalty strength and cut off by a likelihood ratio test [@steiert2016l1]. For the other four compounds it
selected nothing: two parameters per compound changed the IKK phosphorylation and the IκBα
transcript turnover found for DCF. Here all five compounds are the groups of a spike-and-slab
random effect: a compound leaves a rate constant unchanged or changes it by a normal draw, with
probability and spread of changes estimated from all compounds together. The L1 scan of the
publication, repeated on the same model and data, is the comparison
([L1 scan](#l1-scan)). Code: `compounds.R`, on the reduced model
of [Profile likelihood](guide-profiles.html); random effects and `em()` are introduced in
[Nonlinear mixed-effects models](guide-nlme.html).

The second part lists the sparse random-effect distributions (spike-and-slab, Dirichlet-process)
and what their fits report; derivations are in [Methods > Sparsity priors](methods-sparsity-priors.html).

```

```

## Compound data

Each compound has a separate control: DCF on the blots and imaging of the first chapters, the other
four on a third blot set with their own untreated, stimulated control. A condition without compound
belongs to no group (`NA` in column `compound`).

```{r compounddata}
```

```{r}
covariates(dataCompounds)
```

## Spike-and-slab random effects

With $\theta_k$ the log rate constant $k$ and $\eta_{ik}$ the change by compound $i$, a condition
with compound $i$ uses $\theta_k + \eta_{ik}$, one without uses $\theta_k$. The spike-and-slab
distribution [@mitchell1988bayesian; @george1993variable] of a change is

$$p(\eta_{ik}) = (1 - \rho)\, \delta(\eta_{ik}) + \rho\, \mathcal{N}(\eta_{ik};\, 0, \tau^2),$$

a spike at 0 with weight $1 - \rho$ and a normal slab of standard deviation $\tau$ with weight
$\rho$. Changes are independent across compounds and rate constants; $\rho$, $\tau$ are shared.
The inclusion probability $\rho$ (`prob_compound`) is the prior probability that a compound changes
a given rate constant, the expected fraction of nonzero changes. The slab standard deviation $\tau$
(`tau_compound`) is the typical size of a change on the log scale: $\tau = 0.7$ means changes by
about a factor of 2 up or down.
`em()` estimates $\theta$, $\rho$ and $\tau$ from the likelihood with the changes integrated out, a
sum over the subsets of changed rate constants
([Methods > Sparsity priors](methods-sparsity-priors.html#approximate-marginal)). The
posterior spike probability $p_0 = \Pr(\eta_{ik} = 0 \mid y)$ near 0 means a change, near the prior
$1 - \rho$ no evidence, above it evidence against a change.

```{r, include = FALSE}
fit <- stored("results/compounds.rds", "compounds.R", envir = new.env())
rateConstants <- length(unique(fit$random$eta))
```

Each compound has `r rateConstants` candidate rate constants, and the subset sum is exact; beyond
a term budget `em()` uses the expectation consistent (EC) approximation
([Methods > Spike and slab](methods-sparsity-priors.html#spike-and-slab)). Comparison with the
L1 penalty: [Methods > Selection of deviations](methods-sparsity-priors.html#selection-of-deviations).

## Joint fit of all compounds

`em()` estimates fixed effects, change modes, $\rho$ and $\tau$ together. `compounds.R` runs 200
starts, the reduced optimum with changes at 0 and 199 around it, redrawing failed starts; `helix.R`
splits them into `distributedComputing()` tasks by `msem(which = )`
([Remote computing](guide-remote-computing.html)):

```{r compoundfit, eval = FALSE}
```

The best fit is saved with a table of all starts:

```{r compoundsave, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
c(value = fit$value, converged = fit$converged, iterations = fit$iterations)
fit$argument[c("prob_compound", "tau_compound")]
fit$coupling
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
couplingText <- switch(fit$coupling %||% "none",
  expectationConsistent = "the expectation consistent (EC) approximation",
  none = "none: every compound is integrated exactly")
hyperText <- sprintf(
  "With $\\rho = %.2f$ a compound changes %.0f of the %d candidate rate constants a priori; with $\\tau = %.2f$ a change is typically a factor of %.1f up or down.",
  fit$argument[["prob_compound"]], fit$argument[["prob_compound"]] * rateConstants, rateConstants,
  fit$argument[["tau_compound"]], exp(fit$argument[["tau_compound"]]))
```

`value` is $-2 \log L$ of the approximate marginal, `iterations` the steps of the joint trust
region of fixed effects and hyperparameters, `coupling` the integral over coupled changes, here
`r couplingText`. `r hyperText` `plotTrace()` draws $-2 \log L$, the step length and $\rho$, $\tau$ per
iteration:

```{r, fig.height = 4}
plotTrace(fit)
```

## Multistart optimization

The objective has local optima. `msem()` redraws a start whose fit fails, e.g. where EC does not
converge. `$multistart` has per start `value`, `converged`, `iterations`, attempts (`tries`) and the
`error` of a start that failed every attempt. The waterfall shows the best 100 starts; a plateau is
one optimum.

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
plotValues(fit, rank(value, ties.method = "first") <= 100)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
ms <- fit$multistart
best <- min(ms$value, na.rm = TRUE)
multistartText <- sprintf(
  "Of the %d starts, %d end within 1 of the best -2 log L, %d did not converge and %d failed.",
  nrow(ms), sum(ms$value < best + 1, na.rm = TRUE), sum(!ms$converged & !is.na(ms$value)),
  sum(is.na(ms$value)))
retriedText <- if (is.null(ms$tries) || !any(ms$tries > 1)) "" else
  sprintf("%d of the starts were drawn again, %d times in all.", sum(ms$tries > 1), sum(ms$tries - 1))
```

`r multistartText` `r retriedText`

Fit sparse deviations with `method = "focei"`. `method = "saem"` also fits spike-and-slab random
effects, but on this model the SAEM starts reach no common optimum, and the best of them ends above
the FOCEI fit in $-2 \log L$ estimated by importance sampling.

## Changes by compound

The changes are no parameters of the fit and are not selected during it. `em(method = "focei")`
maximizes over $\theta$, $\rho$, $\tau$ the marginal likelihood, per compound $i$ the sum over all
subsets $S$ of the $K$ candidate rate constants,

$$L_i = \sum_S \rho^{\lvert S \rvert} (1 - \rho)^{K - \lvert S \rvert}
\int p(y_i \mid \theta, \eta_S)\, \mathcal{N}(\eta_S;\, 0, \tau^2 I)\, d\eta_S,$$

with $\eta_S$ the changes in $S$, all others 0, and the data term expanded to second order at the
joint mode of the changes, so that every term is a Gaussian integral
([Methods > Spike and slab](methods-sparsity-priors.html#spike-and-slab)). At the estimates every
subset has a posterior weight, the term of the subset divided by $L_i$. The posterior inclusion
probability $1 - p_0$ of the change $\eta_{ik}$ is the summed weight of the subsets that contain
$k$. Two readings follow from these weights:

- the most probable subset per compound, which `fit$random` reports: `cluster` above 0 and `mode`
  the slab mean for the changes in it, 0 for the others;
- a threshold on $p_0$: here a change counts as selected at $p_0 < 0.05$, a posterior inclusion
  probability above 0.95.

The most probable subset also takes up changes the data leave open, with $p_0$ near $1 - \rho$;
the threshold keeps only those the data require.

```{r, include = FALSE}
perGroup <- function(keep) table(factor(fit$random$group[keep], levels = sort(unique(fit$random$group))))
mostProbable <- perGroup(fit$random$cluster > 0)
selectedCount <- perGroup(fit$random$p0 < 0.05)
countText <- sprintf("The most probable subsets hold %s changes, the threshold keeps %s.",
                     enumerate(sprintf("%d (%s)", mostProbable, names(mostProbable))),
                     enumerate(sprintf("%d", selectedCount)))
```

`r countText` Changes with $p_0 < 0.05$, with log-scale modes:

```{r}
changes <- fit$random[fit$random$p0 < 0.05, c("group", "eta", "mode", "se", "p0")]
changes <- changes[order(changes$group, changes$p0), ]
rownames(changes) <- NULL
changes
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
compounds <- sort(unique(fit$random$group))
rates <- unique(fit$random$eta)
counts <- table(factor(changes$group, levels = compounds))
others <- setdiff(compounds, "DCF")
changesText <- sprintf("DCF changes %d of the %d rate constants, %s.",
  counts[["DCF"]], length(rates), enumerate(sprintf("%s %d", others, counts[others])))
# the seven DCF-specific rate constants of the publication, by reaction
publication <- c(act_Ikk_by_TNF = "IKK activation by TNFα", trigger_iIkk = "IKK recovery",
                 act_pIkk = "IKK phosphorylation", act_Ikb_by_Ikk = "IκBα phosphorylation by pIKK",
                 prod_mIkb_by_nNfk = "IκBα transcription", degrad_mIkb = "IκBα transcript degradation",
                 build_A20 = "A20 translation")
reactions <- c(publication, shuttle_RnaA20 = "the delay of the A20 transcript")
named <- function(x) ifelse(x %in% names(reactions), paste0(reactions[x], " (`", x, "`)"), paste0("`", x, "`"))
dcf <- changes$eta[changes$group == "DCF"]
shared <- intersect(names(publication), dcf)
publicationText <- paste0(
  sprintf("Of the %d DCF-specific rate constants of the publication, the spike and slab finds %d: %s",
          length(publication), length(shared), enumerate(named(shared))),
  if (length(setdiff(names(publication), dcf)))
    sprintf("; not %s", enumerate(named(setdiff(names(publication), dcf)))),
  if (length(setdiff(dcf, names(publication))))
    sprintf(", but %s", enumerate(named(setdiff(dcf, names(publication))))),
  ".")
```

`r changesText` The publication kept the 11 differences that vanished last in the L1 scan for DCF,
at the penalty strength beyond which the likelihood ratio test against the model with all
differences rejects at $p < 0.001$, and merged differences whose paths over the penalty strength
coincide, since a change of either has the same effect on the data; seven independent ones remained
[@oppelt2018model]. `r publicationText`

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6.5}
plotRandomEffects(fit, type = "inclusion")
```

Each tile is one $\eta_{ik}$; rate constants follow the pathway from IKK (top) to A20 (bottom).
The fill is the posterior probability of a change, $1 - p_0$; a label is the log-scale value of a
change in the most probable structure, $-0.7$ halves a rate constant. A tile without label has the
spike in that structure, `no data` marks a rate constant that no data of the compound reach, at
the prior $\rho$.

## L1 scan

The method of the publication on the same objective: every change $\eta_{ik}$ is a parameter of the
fit, and the penalty $\lambda \sum_{ik} \lvert \eta_{ik} \rvert$ [@tibshirani1996regression; @steiert2016l1] is added
to $-2 \log L$, one $\lambda$ for all compounds. `trustL1()` sets changes exactly to 0
([L1 penalties](guide-optimization.html#l1-penalties)). For each $\lambda$ of a grid, two starts,
the spike-and-slab estimates and the start of the joint fit with all changes at 0, each run one
fit; the better penalized value counts. The changes it keeps are fitted again without the penalty,
the others fixed at 0. As in the publication, the likelihood ratio test of each refit against the
refit with all changes selects the largest $\lambda$ at which it does not reject at $p < 0.001$.
Changes that reach no data of the compound stay at 0:

```{r compoundsL1, eval = FALSE}
```

`compoundsL1fit` and `compoundsL1refit` run the fits, one per task, and `compoundsL1save` saves the
scan:

```{r}
l1 <- stored("results/compoundsL1.rds", "compounds.R", envir = new.env())
l1$scan
```

`changes` is the number of nonzero changes at $\lambda$, `penalized` $-2 \log L$ without the penalty
at the penalized estimates, `refit` that of the refit, `p` the likelihood ratio test against the
refit with all changes. At $\lambda = 0$ the fit stops at the iteration limit in directions the
data leave nearly flat; the refit from there converges. The paths of the changes over $\lambda$ at
the penalized estimates, red for the changes kept at the selected $\lambda$ (dashed):

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4}
lookup <- setNames(fit$random$eta, fit$random$parameter)
groupOf <- setNames(fit$random$group, fit$random$parameter)
paths <- data.frame(lambda = rep(as.numeric(rownames(l1$path)), ncol(l1$path)),
                    parameter = rep(colnames(l1$path), each = nrow(l1$path)),
                    value = as.vector(l1$path))
paths$compound <- groupOf[paths$parameter]
paths$selected <- paths$parameter %in% l1$selected$parameter
ggplot2::ggplot(paths, ggplot2::aes(lambda, value, group = parameter)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = l1$lambda, linetype = 2, color = "gray50") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = paths[!paths$selected, ], color = "gray75") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = paths[paths$selected, ], color = "#b2182b") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ compound, nrow = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_sqrt(breaks = c(0, 10, 30, 60, 100)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = expression(lambda), y = "change [log]") +
  theme_dMod()
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
ss <- fit$random$parameter[fit$random$p0 < 0.05]
lasso <- l1$selected$parameter
both <- intersect(ss, lasso)
byCompound <- function(x) table(factor(groupOf[x], levels = compounds))
onlyL1 <- setdiff(lasso, ss)
sizeL1 <- abs(setNames(l1$selected$value, lasso)[onlyL1])
l1Text <- sprintf(
  "At $\\lambda = %g$ the scan keeps %d changes, %s. The spike and slab selects %d, %s. Of the %d changes only the scan keeps, %d are below 0.1 on the log scale at the penalized estimates, the largest is %.2f.",
  l1$lambda, length(lasso), enumerate(sprintf("%d (%s)", byCompound(lasso), compounds)), length(ss),
  if (length(both) == length(ss)) "all of them kept by the scan as well" else
    sprintf("%d of them kept by the scan as well", length(both)),
  length(onlyL1), sum(sizeL1 < 0.1), max(sizeL1))
dcfL1 <- lookup[lasso[groupOf[lasso] == "DCF"]]
sharedL1 <- intersect(names(publication), dcfL1)
publicationL1Text <- sprintf(
  "For DCF the scan keeps %d of the %d DCF-specific rate constants of the publication and %d others.",
  length(sharedL1), length(publication), length(setdiff(dcfL1, names(publication))))
```

`r l1Text` `r publicationL1Text`

The L1 penalty shrinks every kept change by the same amount and makes up for it with more small
changes; the likelihood ratio test then counts each of them as a degree of freedom. The spike and
slab leaves the size of a change to the slab and decides a change by the posterior weight of the
subsets with and without it, so it keeps fewer and larger changes and gives each a probability
([Methods > Selection of deviations](methods-sparsity-priors.html#selection-of-deviations)). The
scan here uses one $\lambda$ for all compounds; the publication scanned DCF alone, on the core
model with 24 differences, and kept 11 [@oppelt2018model].

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6.5}
selection <- fit$random[, c("group", "eta", "parameter")]
selection$data <- fit$random$data %||% TRUE
inSS <- selection$parameter %in% ss
inL1 <- selection$parameter %in% lasso
selection$selection <- factor(ifelse(!selection$data, "no data",
  ifelse(inSS & inL1, "both", ifelse(inSS, "spike and slab", ifelse(inL1, "L1", "neither")))),
  levels = c("both", "spike and slab", "L1", "neither", "no data"))
selection$eta <- factor(selection$eta, levels = rev(rates))
selection$publication <- selection$group == "DCF" & selection$eta %in% names(publication)
ggplot2::ggplot(selection, ggplot2::aes(group, eta)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(ggplot2::aes(fill = selection), color = "gray85") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = selection[selection$publication, ], shape = 4, size = 3) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(both = "#2166ac", `spike and slab` = "#67a9cf",
                                        L1 = "#ef8a62", neither = "gray92", `no data` = "white")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_dMod() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Tiles: selection of $\eta_{ik}$ by the spike and slab ($p_0 < 0.05$) and by the L1 scan at the
selected $\lambda$; crosses: the DCF-specific rate constants of the publication.

## Distribution of the changes

Under the model the changes of all compounds, each drawn from the conditional distribution given
the data, follow the prior: spike of mass $1 - \rho$ at 0, slab $\rho\, \mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$.
`plotRandomEffects()` draws them per rate constant, the exact zeros as a bar of their own, against
the prior in red, the prior spike as a cap at the height of a bar of area $1 - \rho$:

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
set.seed(1)
plotRandomEffects(fit, draws = 200)
```

A rate constant with more zeros than the prior spike changes in fewer compounds than $\rho$
says, one with a wide slab part by more than $\tau$.

## Accuracy of the approximation

The marginal of `em()` expands the data at the joint mode of the changes. `logLik(fit, method =
"importance")` estimates it at the same estimates without that expansion, by importance sampling
on the model: per compound 5000 draws from the mixture of the approximation with widened spreads,
weighted by data likelihood times prior. `compounds.R` saves the result:

```{r compoundcheck, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
check <- stored("results/compoundsCheck.rds", "compounds.R", envir = new.env())
data.frame(method = c("approximation", "importance sampling"),
           logLik = c(attr(check, "approximation"), as.numeric(check)),
           se = c(NA, attr(check, "se")))
round(attr(check, "ess"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
gapText <- sprintf(
  "The approximation lies %.1f above the log-likelihood by importance sampling, %.1f per compound, at a standard error of %.2f: a shift of the value on the scale of the error of a Laplace expansion on a nonlinear model.",
  attr(check, "approximation") - as.numeric(check),
  (attr(check, "approximation") - as.numeric(check)) / length(attr(check, "ess")), attr(check, "se"))
```

The last line is the effective sample size of the draws per compound. `r gapText`

## Data and fit by compound

Prediction per compound at the estimated fixed effects and changes against the compound data, each
point with the measured standard deviation, which the blots have in place of an error model; gray:
the untreated, stimulated control of the same blots at the fixed effects alone. DCF blots span six
hours, the others 50 minutes:

::: {.wide}
```{r, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8.5}
outer <- getParameters(prdCompounds)
estimates <- c(fit$argument, fit$fixed, setNames(fit$random$mode, fit$random$parameter))
pars <- setNames(numeric(length(outer)), outer)
pars[intersect(outer, names(estimates))] <- estimates[intersect(outer, names(estimates))]

treated <- grep("^TNF_[A-Z]", names(dataCompounds), value = TRUE)
controls <- sub("^TNF_[A-Z]+_", "TNF_none_", treated)
observed <- as.data.frame(dataCompounds)
times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 60, length.out = 200), seq(0, max(observed$time), length.out = 200))))
prediction <- as.data.frame(prdCompounds(times, pars, deriv = FALSE, conditions = union(treated, controls)))

# every compound with the untreated control on the same blots
blots <- c("IkBa", "pIkBa", "pIKK", "pNFkB")
byCompound <- function(frame) do.call(rbind, Map(function(cond, ctl) {
  rows <- frame[frame$condition %in% c(cond, ctl) & frame$name %in% blots,
                c("time", "name", "value", "sigma", "condition")]
  rows$compound <- sub("^TNF_([A-Z]+)_.*", "\\1", cond)
  rows$treatment <- ifelse(rows$condition == cond, "compound", "control")
  rows
}, treated, controls))
points <- byCompound(observed)
# the curves over the time range of the data of the compound
curves <- byCompound(prediction)
curves <- curves[curves$time <= tapply(points$time, points$compound, max)[curves$compound], ]
colors <- c(compound = "#b2182b", control = "gray55")
ggplot2::ggplot(mapping = ggplot2::aes(time, value, color = treatment)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = curves) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(data = points, ggplot2::aes(ymin = value - sigma, ymax = value + sigma),
                         width = 0) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = points) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(name ~ compound, scales = "free") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3)) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "time [min]", y = "log signal [a.u.]", color = NULL) +
  theme_dMod() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Sparse random-effect distributions

`gr(group, dist = )` sets the random-effect distribution of a term. Besides `normal()`, two have
deviations exactly zero unless the data need them:

| distribution | a deviation $\eta$ of a group | hyperparameters |
|---|---|---|
| `spikeSlab()` | $0$ with probability $1 - \rho$, else $\mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$ | `prob_<grouping>`, `tau_<grouping>` |
| `dirichletProcess()` | cluster value: $0$ for the population cluster, else one $\mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$ draw | `concentration_<grouping>`, `tau_<grouping>` |

Hyperparameters are shared by the symbols of a term, numbered `_1`, `_2`, ... for several terms
of one grouping, and estimated with the fixed effects unless given, as in `spikeSlab(tau = 0.5)`.
A spike-and-slab deviation is zero with a probability reported per group. Under the Dirichlet process groups share deviations in clusters with the population
value, see [Dirichlet-process random effects](#dirichlet-process-random-effects). Normal and sparse
random effects of one grouping combine; `em(method = "focei")` fits all.

## Fitting sparse random effects

`em(method = "focei")` integrates sparse random effects on the Laplace approximation of the data
term at the joint mode of a group, exactly where possible, the spike-and-slab effects of a group
jointly even where the data couple them, and by EC where the data link a Dirichlet-process effect
to another factor or the subset sum leaves the budget. Fixed
effects and hyperparameters move in one trust region: no EM iteration count, no random numbers.
`fit$coupling` is `"expectationConsistent"` if a group needed EC, `NULL` if all are exact. Integral,
gradient and hyperparameter steps:
[Methods > Approximate marginal](methods-sparsity-priors.html#approximate-marginal),
[Methods > Expectation consistent
approximation](methods-sparsity-priors.html#expectation-consistent-approximation) and
[Methods > Joint trust region](methods-sparsity-priors.html#joint-trust-region).

| entry of `control$sparseFit` | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `maxOuter` | `200` | joint trust-region iterations, all runs |
| `trustControl` | `rinit = 1`, `rmax = 10`, `ftol = 1e-10`, `mtol = 1e-5` | joint trust region, as `trust()` |

Other entries are an error. The compound fit passes the `tolerances` of
[Setting up models](guide-model.html) in `trustControl`, above the solver error in value and gradient. A run stopping
short of `mtol` restarts while runs lower $-2 \log L$ by more than `mtol`. `msem()` perturbs
concentrations and slab standard deviations on log scale, slab probabilities on logit scale.

## Reported structure

The fit reports the most probable structure: subset of deviations (spike and slab) or partition
(Dirichlet process). Spike deviations are exactly zero, slab deviations the posterior mean given
the structure ([Methods > Reported structure](methods-sparsity-priors.html#reported-structure)).
`fit$random` has a row per group and random effect:

- `mode`, this value;
- `se`, posterior standard deviation over spike and slab;
- spike-and-slab and Dirichlet process: `cluster`, 0 for the population value, 1, 2, ... for
  deviating groups or clusters in group order, and `p0`, posterior probability of zero deviation;
- `data`, whether the random effect reaches data of the group, where some do not.

A sparse random effect reaching no data of the group (through transformations, ODE, observables,
error model) rests at 0 with the prior standard deviation and, for spike and slab,
$p_0 = 1 - \rho$. `fit$slab` lists probabilities, concentrations and slab standard deviations,
each with term symbols, estimate and whether fixed.

## Standard errors

With spike-and-slab random effects `fit$hessian` is `NULL`; `vcov()` inverts
`fit$information`, the empirical information from the group scores plus that of the conditions
without random effects and the priors, their expected information (`hessian = "expected"`), which
is positive semidefinite also with an error model. It needs more groups than parameters, or those
terms for the other directions; otherwise `vcov()` is an error and standard errors are `NA`. `fit$information` is not a Hessian of the
marginal, and the eigenvalues of the matrix say nothing about a saddle point. In the compound fit `r seText`. `dirichletProcess()` fits have neither;
`confint(method = "profile")` gives intervals. Details: [Methods > Standard errors](methods-sparsity-priors.html#standard-errors).

## Dirichlet-process random effects

With `gr(group, dist = dirichletProcess())` groups and population value form clusters; the
concentration $\alpha$ sets how readily a group opens a new one. The population cluster has
deviation zero, every other cluster one common deviation from $\mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$. $\alpha$ and
$\tau$ are estimated by marginal maximum likelihood in one fit, with no penalty to scan. The
reported structure is that of spike and slab with clusters in place of single deviations; the
compounds here are fitted without it.

`method = "focei"` sums exactly over partitions of up to 14 groups. `method = "saem"` draws
partitions, allowing normal random effects alongside but no other sparse ones, and reports the most
frequent partition of the late draws, from `window` iterations after burn-in, with standard error
`valueSE` of $-2 \log L$.
`control$saem$particles` sets the importance-sampling particles, default 500; `converged` says
whether burn-in ended by the drift test. An SAEM fit has no gradient, Hessian or empirical
information. Details:
[Methods > Sparsity priors](methods-sparsity-priors.html#dirichlet-process-random-effects).

Reference: `randomEffects()`, `spikeSlab()`, `dirichletProcess()`, `em()`, `msem()`,
`plotValues()`, `plotTrace()`, `plotRandomEffects()`, `plotPars()`
